t.E507.agn: In 2019, EFSA re-evaluated hydrochloric acid and potassium, calcium and magnesium chlorides together; for the assessment it used a reference value of 40 mg chloride/kg body weight per day based on human data, and found no concern regarding genotoxicity or carcinogenicity. Mean exposure was below or equal to this value in all age groups; it has been reported that in some young age groups it may be slightly exceeded in high consumers (95th percentile). EFSA found no safety concern at the reported uses and use levels. In 1965, JECFA had set the ADI as 'not limited'.
t.E507.body: In the gastrointestinal tract it dissociates into chloride and the accompanying ions. Chloride taken in with food is almost completely absorbed along the intestine and distributed to organs and tissues; the amount in the body is regulated by balance mechanisms, and it is excreted mainly in urine, and also in sweat and faeces.
t.E507.found.0: May be used at quantum satis (as much as needed) in many foods in the EU
t.E507.prod: It is produced chemically, mostly as a by-product of chlorination processes, or by the reaction of hydrogen with chlorine.
t.E507.regx.0: Re-evaluated; a reference value of 40 mg chloride/kg body weight per day was used; no safety concern at the reported uses.
t.E507.regx.2: Group I additive; generally permitted at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E507.summary: Hydrochloric acid (spirit of salt). In food production it is used to regulate acidity and to break down starch or protein.
t.E507.what: It is a strong mineral acid used to regulate acidity.
